glosses: To express one’s sympathetic pleasure or joy to the person(s) it is felt for; to felicitate.

examples.text: Remind me to congratulate Dave and Lisa on their wedding.
We must congratulate Dave and Lisa on getting married.

Ronaldo Sr., who is the record goalscorer in men’s international soccer with 136 goals for Portugal, congratulated his son on his Instagram Stories by posting a picture of his name on the squad list, saying: “Proud of you, son!”

glosses: To consider oneself fortunate in some matter.

examples.text: I congratulated myself on the success of my plan.

glosses: An expression of praise, congratulation, or respect.

examples.text: pay someone a compliment

[…] I met him
With customary compliment; when he,
Wafting his eyes to the contrary and falling
A lip of much contempt, speeds from me and
So leaves me to consider what is breeding
That changeth thus his manners.

[...] what honour that,
but tedious waste of time, to sit and hear
So many hollow compliments and lies,
Outlandish flatteries?

Virtue indeed meets many a rhiming friend,
And many a compliment politely penn’d,

glosses: Complimentary language; courtesy, flattery.

examples.text: He told the Captain, He was heartily sorry for his Misfortunes; tho’ in my Opinion that was nothing but a Compliment: For, as I found afterwards, he was more brutish, and dishonest, than most of the other Kings on the Island […]
